- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects; reduce subsequent forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.  
- If true price shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 50% of 30d moving avg), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent trend reversal.  
- For 30d horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven volatility; if sentiment swings sharply, adjust forecast to reflect sentiment direction within 2–3 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment phase; align forecast to sentiment’s most recent dominant polarity.
